result.title: LIRA: A More Interpretable Dynamic Loss-Informed Rank Allocation for Low-Rank Adaptation
result.summary: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) has become a widely used parameter-efficient fine-tuning method for large pretrained models. However, standard LoRA typically assigns a fixed rank profile despite layer- and stage-dependent adaptation needs, while recent adaptive-rank variants often rely on heuristic or first-order signals that provide only an indirect link between rank reallocation and local loss behavior. This leaves the rationale behind each rank reallocation insufficiently interpretable. Motivated by this gap, we propose LIRA (Loss-Informed Rank Allocation), a dynamic-rank LoRA method designed to make online rank reallocation more interpretable. LIRA scores each layer by the estimated magnitude of the local loss perturbation associated with its recent LoRA-factor movements under a second-order approximation, making the basis for each rank change interpretable term by term. By periodically applying DELTA (Displacement-Evaluated Loss-Trajectory Allocation), a displacement-based algorithm for LoRA rank reallocation, LIRA produces discrete effective ranks under matched budgets while remaining compatible with standard (A,B) adapters. On RoBERTa-base GLUE under the La-LoRA/LoRA protocol, LIRA outperforms the uniform-LoRA and adaptive-rank baselines reported under this protocol; Trajectory EMA attains performance competitive with Fixed-point Fisher at lower estimation cost.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 LIRA，一种动态秩分配的 LoRA 方法：用二阶近似估计各层 LoRA 因子近期移动引起的局部损失扰动幅度来给层打分，并周期性通过基于位移的 DELTA 算法重分配秩，在 RoBERTa-base GLUE 上优于均匀秩与若干自适应秩基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用局部损失扰动幅度为各模块的容量/更新分配提供可解释依据，可能可供核查是否可类比用于 latent 推理中的贡献分配与计算预算调度，但原文未涉及多模态或推理期状态。
